tasks.short: Help customers resolve technical problems with purchased products.

steps.what: Clarify the symptoms, operating conditions and urgency with the customer.
Find the installed product, relevant manuals, warranty terms and previous support records.
Assess likely causes and decide whether specialist escalation is needed.
Explain approved troubleshooting steps and agree follow-up or specialist involvement.
Record the outcome and assign follow-up to the responsible colleague.

loop.input: Representative's notes, support outcome and follow-up commitment.
loop.output: Draft support record with proposed owner and due date.
loop.check: Representative checks technical statements and commitments; code validates customer, owner and date.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per case; missing facts return to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary; templates cannot reliably turn them into a useful case summary.

tasks.design: An answer desk joins customer and product identifiers across {CRM}, {ERP}, {HELPDESK} and versioned manuals in {DOCS}. The representative diagnoses and approves advice; a bounded drafting loop prepares the support record, while {WORKFLOW} assigns approved follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Installed-product records and manuals sit apart, and technical advice depends on operating context.
tasks.enabler_now: Search indexes, record links and small drafting loops can be assembled more cheaply with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete installation records, obsolete manuals and safety-critical faults require experienced people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise misleading symptoms, establish trust and know when the customer should stop operating equipment.

ambition.what: Scheduled post-installation troubleshooting clinics for smaller customer accounts.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence hunting and record entry, leaving room for scheduled troubleshooting clinics. Technical approval rights stay within existing competence limits.

reach.task: Prepare a reproducible fault description for specialist diagnosis.
reach.learn: Operating-condition capture, fault isolation and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Record-backed answers and escalation beyond manuals fit a deterministic answer desk.
Incorrect customer-facing automated answers can create liability; the cited case concerns airline fares, not technical support.
Customer-facing AI interaction requires disclosure under the cited AI Act provision.

assumptions: The representative handles first-line support and escalates specialist cases.
The proposed answer desk is internal; a customer-facing extension needs AI disclosure where applicable.
GDPR applies to customer records. National rules apply to employee monitoring and consultation.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The conversation remains the largest component despite substantial gains in retrieval and paperwork.
unknowns: Whether installed products have reliable customer and version identifiers.
Which technical advice the representative may approve.
Whether current manuals and support records are accessible through supported interfaces.
Whether national consultation or consent requirements apply to the intended logging.
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered directly from approved records?
Which fault categories require immediate specialist escalation?
How often does retrieval select the wrong product revision?
new_work: Review drafted support records and commitments.
Resolve missing product identifiers and stale manual links.
Maintain escalation rules and test retrieval against known faults.

tasks.short: Advise customers how to use products to improve their production process.

steps.what: Discuss production goals, constraints and current product use.
Observe the process and ask operators about practical problems.
Calculate throughput, consumption or quality differences for feasible usage options.
Choose a recommendation within approved operating limits.
Explain trade-offs and agree a controlled trial with the customer.
Write the trial plan and record its measures, responsibilities and review date.

loop.input: Approved recommendation, trial agreement and calculated option comparison.
loop.output: Draft trial plan using a fixed template.
loop.check: Code copies numerical limits unchanged; representative checks measures, responsibilities and agreement fidelity.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported instructions or missing agreement details require manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but agreed trial details arrive as variable free text.

tasks.design: A deterministic calculator in {WORKFLOW} combines customer measurements with approved specifications from {DOCS} and produces an option comparison. The representative chooses the recommendation and secures customer agreement; a bounded loop drafts the trial plan, and {CRM} schedules its review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Production conditions differ between customers, and calculations often depend on locally maintained assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculators, validated input forms and document templates are cheaper to build and connect.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable measurements, causal attribution and safe changes to a running production process remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: See the process in context, question apparent gains and negotiate a trial operators can actually run.

ambition.what: Measured product-usage trials with a scheduled results review.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time calculating and writing, and more time reviewing trial results with customers. Authority over customer production changes remains with the customer.

reach.learn: Baseline selection, measurement uncertainty and safe operating limits.

evidence.claim: Calculators can automate arithmetic while site assessment and final usage choices remain judgement steps.
Elfsquad provides product-rule configuration connected to sales and finance records; this supports selection, not production diagnosis.

assumptions: Advice concerns product use within documented limits.
The representative can recommend routine usage changes; specialist changes require a sales engineer.
Customer production data is confidential. GDPR applies when records identify people.
Access and consultation follow national rules where applicable.
Time and build estimates are provisional; observation and conversation dominate as the supplied priors suggest.
unknowns: Which production measurements customers can provide reliably.
Which usage changes require specialist approval.
Whether approved calculation methods already exist.
Whether customers permit storage of process observations and measurements.
research_questions: Which recurring usage decisions have stable formulas and operating limits?
What baseline makes a trial result credible?
Which apparent improvements introduce quality or safety trade-offs?
new_work: Validate calculator assumptions and update specifications.
Review draft trial plans before sending.
Handle incomplete measurements and conflicting trial results.

tasks.short: Study new technical products and understand where they fit customer needs.

steps.what: Collect current manuals, specifications and release information for the new product.
Read specifications, capabilities, limitations and differences from existing products.

loop.input: Versioned study pack and existing product specifications.
loop.output: Cited reading guide with product differences, limitations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Code verifies cited passages and numerical values; representative reads critical source sections.
loop.stop: One guide and one correction per product version; unreadable or conflicting sources stay flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technical differences and caveats are expressed across varied prose and tables.

steps.what: Discuss unresolved questions in supplier training or with a technical colleague.
Identify suitable customer applications and cases requiring specialist help.
Organise learning notes and references for future customer discussions.

loop.input: Study notes, clarified limits, application notes and source references.
loop.output: Structured product learning note with open questions and source links.
loop.check: Representative checks meaning and limitations; code verifies links and product version.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; uncited claims remain questions rather than facts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Personal notes and training clarifications need language synthesis beyond fixed field copying.

tasks.design: Configured subscriptions collect approved product versions from {PARTNER_PORTAL} into {DOCS}. A bounded reading loop prepares a cited guide and organises reviewed learning notes; the representative studies critical sections, asks technical questions and evaluates applications against customer requirements in {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier documents vary in structure, and useful caveats are scattered across revisions and training notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexing and bounded summarisation can produce source-linked reading guides at modest cost.
tasks.still_hard: A concise guide cannot establish technical competence or resolve ambiguous specifications.
tasks.human_edge: Understand mechanisms, recognise missing knowledge and transfer learning to unfamiliar customer situations.

ambition.what: Review new-product suitability for active technical opportunities after each product release.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less document collection and note organisation, with more focused study and application reviews. No additional technical sign-off rights are gained.

reach.task: Screen whether a new product fits a customer's technical requirements.
reach.learn: Specification interpretation, compatibility constraints and evidence-based questioning.

evidence.claim: Source-linked reading guides can reduce searching and note preparation while substantive learning remains human.
The digest provides no documented case measuring technical product-learning gains for this occupation.

assumptions: Supplier documents can be accessed and processed under existing permissions.
Learning notes support study; approved manuals remain the authority for customer advice.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer requirements. Employee learning analytics may trigger national consultation rules.
Time and build estimates are provisional; document reading remains the largest step.
Configured document subscriptions are available; unsupported supplier access would require additional integration.
unknowns: Whether suppliers expose versioned documents and change notices.
Which materials may be processed by a model.
Whether formal certification or assessed training is required.
Who validates technical interpretations before they become shared guidance.
research_questions: Which specification changes are most often missed by representatives?
Can reading guides preserve every critical limitation?
Does assisted study improve application screening without reducing understanding?
new_work: Check citations, limitations and unresolved questions.
Replace stale guides when product versions change.
Maintain document permissions and release subscriptions.
Seek specialist clarification for conflicting technical statements.

tasks.short: Select, stock and distribute product samples and approved educational materials.

steps.what: Choose appropriate samples and approved materials for the customer visit.
Check physical availability, condition and expiry of the selected resources.
Request reserved samples, packing materials or replenishment from the warehouse.
Pick, pack and label samples and printed materials.
Deliver resources during the visit and explain their intended use.
Record issued quantities and update sample inventory.
Re-enter delivered resources against the customer record.

tasks.design: Configure sample availability, reservations and replenishment in {OPS_SYSTEM}, with approved material versions linked from {DOCS}. A request flow in {WORKFLOW} replaces mailbox coordination, and a delivery event updates inventory and {CRM} together; people retain physical inspection, packing and customer explanation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample inventory and customer activity records are disconnected, while physical work limits total savings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inventory configuration and a small event integration can remove coordination and duplicate entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, storage requirements, missing stock and restricted samples still need people.
tasks.human_edge: Choose useful resources, inspect them properly and explain what the customer can safely learn from them.

ambition.what: A standard sample-request service for smaller technical prospects.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time requesting and recording resources; physical work remains substantial. A wider sample service requires an agreed budget, and no automatic spending rights are gained.

reach.task: Coordinate sample reservations and delivery exceptions.
reach.learn: Inventory movements, fulfilment statuses and restricted-item handling.

evidence.claim: Inventory configuration and dispatch-event integration can remove routine sample coordination and duplicate records.
The digest provides no documented case for automating physical sample handling.

assumptions: Samples are tracked as inventory items, including zero-price issues where appropriate.
Routine sample selection is permitted within existing budget and handling limits.
Time shares include warehouse participation in the task, rather than only the representative's effort.
Physical steps account for 70% of today's task time, consistent with the supplied means prior.
GDPR applies to customer delivery records. National rules govern any employee-monitoring consultation.
Time and build ranges are planning estimates; no model loop is needed.
unknowns: Whether sample stock is recorded reliably in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Which samples have expiry, storage, transport or recipient restrictions.
Whether representatives or warehouse staff usually pack resources.
Whether delivery confirmation can be captured during the visit.
Whether stock events can update {CRM} through supported interfaces.
research_questions: Which sample categories can use standard reservation and replenishment rules?
Where do inventory discrepancies arise between issue and delivery?
Which printed materials could be replaced by customer-requested digital copies?
new_work: Capture delivery confirmation and report damaged or missing samples.
Maintain sample restrictions, stock thresholds and approved material versions.
Review demand and budget before expanding the sample service.

role.altitude: The representative becomes better prepared for technical conversations through faster retrieval, calculations and paperwork. Diagnosis, production advice and customer commitments remain within existing competence and delegated authority.
reach: Sales engineer: prepare fault evidence and design measurable usage trials.
Order clerk: coordinate sample fulfilment and inventory exceptions.
Sales manager: present evidence from technical trials for account prioritisation.
role.ambitious_version: Offer smaller technical customers a structured service combining post-installation clinics, measured usage trials and suitable sample packs, supported by shared records and approved technical evidence.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
